title: Finite common-word OS versus direct D/delta-D route bridge
question: Does the finite OS common-word context decay seen in EXP-001174/001175 align with the direct D/delta-D route, or do the finite OS deltas decrease while direct seminorm maxima grow with volume?
method: Read only the committed EXP-001175 direction/source run pair, the EXP-001169 extended direct D/delta-D run pair and the EXP-001149 source-weighted direct run pair; verify PASS verdicts and exploration IDs before analysis.
Group the EXP-001175 adjacent path comparisons by endpoint-left, center and endpoint-right role at beta=0.25 and retain both path4->path5 and path5->path6 maximum context deltas.
Extract the EXP-001169 volume-4/volume-6 D_norm and delta_D_norm maxima and the EXP-001149 amplitude-one source-weighted Gibbs D and delta_H_D maxima at volumes 2,4,6.
Compute finite monotonicity predicates, endpoint symmetry absolute differences, and last/first ratios. Treat all ratios as descriptive diagnostics rather than shared norms or asymptotic constants.
Run the same aggregation independently on the independent upstream runs and use an integrated verifier with Lean R247 and scope firewalls.
decision_reason: The bridge exposes a mixed finite signal instead of conflating two route diagnostics. All three EXP-001175 source-role OS context sequences decrease, and endpoint-left/right absolute delta differences are about 3.33e-16. In contrast, the EXP-001169 direct D and delta-D maxima increase from volume 4 to 6 by last/first ratios 1.002580664886537 and 1.0029230653778658, while EXP-001149 source-weighted Gibbs D and delta_H_D maxima increase from volume 2 to 6 by ratios 2.4477906160754466 and 6.577274347073025. The finite data therefore support a targeted analytic bridge estimate but do not close either Cauchy route.
finding: Primary 10/10 and independent 10/10 assertions pass; the integrated verifier passes 28/28 with Lean R247 PASS. The OS role sequences at beta=0.25 are center 1.994630439627887e-05 -> 4.9703497650988027e-08, endpoint-left 1.3494971806693457e-10 -> 3.516076318987871e-13, and endpoint-right 1.3494938500002718e-10 -> 3.519406988061746e-13. Direct route maxima retain finite volume growth, and source-weighted direct values grow more strongly. The bridge is provenance-linked and claim-nonbearing; uniform common-word, direct D/delta-D Cauchy and common-alpha flags remain false.
next_action: Seek an analytic inequality that relates the OS word seminorm to a direct weighted D/delta-D norm with explicit source-distance, degree, volume, cutoff and beta factors. Do not infer that finite OS decay repairs the unclosed direct Cauchy gate.

adversarial_review.check: Only committed PASS JSON inputs from EXP-001149, EXP-001169 and EXP-001175 are read, with exploration IDs checked before aggregation.
OS Gram context deltas and direct D/delta-D maxima are explicitly different finite diagnostics; no common norm is assumed.
Declared path and source-weight volume labels are retained separately; no finite list is called an exhaustion sequence.
Increase/decrease predicates are computed from recorded arrays and are not promoted to asymptotic estimates.
Direct maxima keep their source, beta, cutoff and finite fixture boundaries; their growth is not a universal no-go for all weighted norms.
The independent bridge uses only independent upstream JSONs and reproduces all bridge fields without importing primary code.
R247 is rerun for exact finite Gibbs/scope checks; bridge arithmetic remains a transparent Python aggregation of committed evidence.
Mixed finite-route behavior neither proves nor refutes a thermodynamic OS state, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

qft_interface.closed: The finite OS context-decay and direct D/delta-D growth diagnostics are provenance-linked, independently reproduced and compared with explicit last/first ratios.
qft_interface.open: An analytic inequality connecting OS word control to a source/volume/cutoff/beta-uniform direct seminorm remains open, as do common-word exhaustion embedding, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum and physical TECT gates.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 route-selection evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite route bridge. It is not a theorem identifying any finite diagnostic with a thermodynamic QFT norm or state.
no_overclaim: This package only re-aggregates committed finite diagnostics. It does not prove a common OS carrier, direct Cauchy convergence, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, a mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
